neighbours.label: 'doing' (or 'do') as the light verb of a hobby or activity after enjoys / loves / permits
fire: In her free time, Clara enjoys doing watercolour painting by the lake.
My grandfather loves doing crossword puzzles over breakfast.
The new role will permit doing research alongside teaching.
Many retirees enjoy doing volunteer work at the local hospital.
He has always liked doing woodwork in his garage on weekends.
Stretch, breathe deeply, do a few squats, it does not matter which.
The children were excited about doing science experiments in class.
She spends her evenings doing yoga and reading novels.
quiet: In her free time, Clara enjoys watercolour paintings of the lake.
My grandfather loves the crossword puzzle in the morning paper.
The new role will include research alongside teaching.
Many retirees enjoy the volunteer lunches at the local hospital.
He has always liked the smell of wood in his garage on weekends.
Stretching and deep breathing are good, it does not matter which.
The children were excited about the science museum trip.
She spends her evenings with a cup of tea and a novel.

notes: Coordinating 'and' between nouns also appears in top examples; the opposite pole is the comma between gerunds.
